claims.text: Get fresh scan data
claims.note: The toolbar button fetches the latest scan data TurfRad holds (see request-scan-data/tile/2 for what it does not do).

claims.text: Request a new TurfRad scan rather than waiting for one.
claims.note: The button does not order a scan. It resets the site's last-update time to two days ago (SpatialAdjustService.cs:992) and starts the background retrieval at once (:998-999). That retrieval downloads the sprinkler statistics TurfRad already holds (:2527). The same retrieval runs by itself whenever the site's update interval has passed (:1949-1958): 1800 seconds by the shipped default (appsettings.json:32), checked every 15 seconds (appsettings.json:27). A new scan exists only when TurfRad has taken one. The product's own tooltip says "Request latest scan data".
claims.developNote: On develop, TurfRad can report that it has nothing newer than the last update. The retrieval then keeps the existing scans and creates today's adjustments from them (develop SpatialAdjustService.cs:2140-2153, :2575). The button still fetches data rather than ordering a scan.
claims.correction: Fetch the latest TurfRad scan data now rather than waiting for the next automatic retrieval. Why: the button starts the retrieval that Spatial Adjust otherwise runs every 30 minutes by default (SpatialAdjustService.cs:978-1002, appsettings.json:32). It does not order a new scan.

claims.text: A stale course is not something you have to wait out.
claims.note: Only partly true. A course whose data is behind TurfRad's may only be waiting for the next automatic retrieval, and the button brings that forward. But the retrieval only fetches what TurfRad holds (SpatialAdjustService.cs:2527), and it runs by itself every 30 minutes by default (:1949-1958, appsettings.json:32). If the scan dates are days old, TurfRad has nothing newer, and nothing in Spatial Adjust changes that.
claims.correction: A course that has fallen behind TurfRad does not have to wait for the next automatic retrieval. Why: the button starts it now (SpatialAdjustService.cs:978-1002). It cannot make a new scan, so if the dates are still old after you reload, TurfRad has nothing newer.

claims.text: Request a new TurfRad scan, and reload when it lands.
claims.note: Same finding as request-scan-data/tile/2. The reload half is right: a banner appears when the retrieval finishes, and Reload Data loads the result.
claims.developNote: On develop, TurfRad can report that it has nothing newer than the last update. The retrieval then keeps the existing scans and creates today's adjustments from them (develop SpatialAdjustService.cs:2140-2153, :2575). The button still fetches data rather than ordering a scan.
claims.correction: Ask for the latest scan data TurfRad holds, and reload when it is ready. Why: the button fetches TurfRad's existing data ahead of schedule (SpatialAdjustService.cs:978-1002, :2527). It does not order a scan.

claims.text: Toolbar
claims.note: The button is in the main Spatial Adjust toolbar, to the right of the pushed-today counter.

claims.text: When a scan is not current the calculation still runs — it runs on a modelled value carried forward from the last scan and the weather since, shown in grey italics.
claims.note: Retyped from prerequisite to behaviour. True under Option 2 only. A station is marked estimated when its scan is not from today and the calculation option is Option 2, Delta Plus Today ET (spatial-adjust-course.model.ts:184-188, sa-table-item.model.ts:68-70). Its moisture reading is then shown in dark grey italics with a calculator icon (sa-table-card.component.html:29-31, sa-table-card.component.less:107-110). When there is no reading from today, the server works from the previous predicted value (SpatialAdjustService.cs:3031-3043). Under Option 1 a stale station is not estimated. With saShowCurrentOnly true on production (environment.toro-prod.ts:87), its % Adj. shows a dash with no input (sa-table-card.component.html:51-62), and it is left out of the pending list (sa-dashboard.component.ts:621-624), so it cannot be pushed.
claims.developNote: On develop the same carry-forward is in CalculateAdjustment (develop SpatialAdjustService.cs:3211-3219). It is also used when TurfRad reports nothing newer (:3312).
claims.correction: When a scan is not current, what you see depends on the calculation option. Under Option 2 the calculation still runs, on a value modelled forward from the last scan and the weather since, and the moisture reading is shown in grey italics with a calculator icon. Under Option 1 the station shows a dash in % Adj. and is left out of the push until a current scan arrives. Why: only Option 2 marks a stale station as estimated (spatial-adjust-course.model.ts:184-188), and production hides stations that are neither current nor estimated (environment.toro-prod.ts:87, sa-table-card.component.html:51-62).

claims.text: Read the scan date before anything else
claims.note: The scan date is on every station row.

claims.text: Every station row carries the date its reading was captured.
claims.note: Station rows show lastScan in small grey type beside the name. A paired row shows the newest date in the pair (sa-dash-table.component.ts:391-396). Area and hole rows show a date in a column of their own (sa-table-card.component.html:36).

claims.text: One stale row is a station; a column of stale dates is the whole course, and that is a supply problem rather than a settings problem.
claims.note: The dates are TurfRad's recorded scan dates (SpatialAdjustService.cs:2999), which no setting changes. Requesting scan data helps only if TurfRad holds something newer (see request-scan-data/tile/2).

claims.text: Scan dates sit beside the station name in the table.
claims.note: Figure caption.

claims.text: Request the latest scan
claims.note: The request is made from the toolbar button.

claims.text: The circular-arrow button in the toolbar’s right-hand group is Request latest scan data.
claims.note: The icon is Font Awesome "sync" (two circular arrows), which spins while a request is outstanding (sa-main-toolbar.component.html:57). The tooltip is SPATIAL_ADJUST.REQUEST_SCAN_DATA through the titlecase pipe, so it shows "Request Latest Scan Data". The button's text label is not displayed (sa-main-toolbar.component.less:163-165) and carries the Settings string, not the scan string (sa-main-toolbar.component.html:58).

claims.text: It asks TurfRad for a new scan; it does not reload the dashboard, and it does not change a single calculation setting.
claims.note: The second and third parts are right: the handler only calls the API and shows a toast (sa-main-toolbar.component.ts:329-343), and no setting is touched. The first part is not. The server resets the site's last-update time and starts the background retrieval (SpatialAdjustService.cs:978-1002), which downloads the sprinkler statistics TurfRad already holds (:2527). Nothing asks TurfRad to scan.
claims.developNote: On develop, TurfRad can report that it has nothing newer than the last update. The retrieval then keeps the existing scans and creates today's adjustments from them (develop SpatialAdjustService.cs:2140-2153, :2575). The button still fetches data rather than ordering a scan.
claims.correction: It asks Spatial Adjust to fetch the latest scan data TurfRad already holds, ahead of the next automatic retrieval. It does not order a new scan, it does not reload the dashboard, and it does not change a single calculation setting. Why: the request only brings the scheduled retrieval forward (SpatialAdjustService.cs:978-1002, :2527).

claims.text: Request latest scan data, between the pushed-today counter and the gear.
claims.note: Figure caption. From the counter the order is: separator, this button, the Announcements bullhorn, the Settings gear. The bullhorn also sits between this button and the gear (sa-main-toolbar.component.html:62-65).

claims.text: Note. This button and Reload Data are two different things.
claims.note: The scan button is in the toolbar. Reload Data appears only on the banner.

claims.text: One asks for new data; the other brings data that has already arrived into the page.
claims.note: "New data" means whatever TurfRad holds that Spatial Adjust has not yet retrieved. Reload Data re-fetches the dashboard's data from the server.

claims.text: It queues, it does not block
claims.note: The endpoint returns 202 Accepted, and the server starts the retrieval without waiting for it.

claims.text: The request is queued and you are told so: retrieval may take several minutes, and you are notified when it is ready.
claims.note: The toast reads "Request Queued", then "Retrieval may take several minutes. We'll notify you when it's ready." The notification is the banner, which appears only if the dashboard is still open when the retrieval finishes (see request-scan-data/3/3).

claims.text: You can carry on reading the table while it runs — nothing is frozen and nothing is lost if you navigate away.
claims.note: Only the button changes while the request runs: it dims and its icon spins (sa-main-toolbar.component.html:52, :57). The retrieval runs on the server and finishes whether or not the page is open, so no data is lost. The banner does depend on the open page. It appears only if the toolbar that made the request is still loaded when the completion signal arrives (sa-main-toolbar.component.ts:207-213). After navigating away no banner comes, and the retrieved data loads the next time the dashboard loads its data (sa-dashboard.component.ts:388).

claims.text: A queued request confirms immediately; the data arrives later.
claims.note: Figure caption.

claims.text: Reload when the banner appears
claims.note: The banner carries the Reload Data button.

claims.text: When the scan lands, a banner says so.
claims.note: The banner marks the end of the retrieval, not the arrival of a scan. The server sends the completion signal after it has processed every course for the site, whether or not TurfRad returned anything new, and even if a course failed (SpatialAdjustService.cs:2054, :2060-2072). The toolbar shows the banner for any completion while a request is outstanding (sa-main-toolbar.component.ts:207-213). The banner reads "The requested scan data is ready." (SPATIAL_ADJUST.REQUESTED_SCAN_DATA_READY).
claims.developNote: On develop the completion signal is unchanged. The banner also appears when TurfRad reports nothing newer (develop SpatialAdjustService.cs:2140-2153).
claims.correction: When the retrieval finishes, a banner says so. It appears whether or not TurfRad had a newer scan, so check the scan dates after you reload. Why: the server signals completion after every retrieval, whether or not there is new data (SpatialAdjustService.cs:2060-2072).

claims.text: Reload Data pulls it into the dashboard and every suggestion recalculates against the new readings.
claims.note: Reload Data re-fetches all of the dashboard's data (sa-dashboard.component.ts:280-286), and each suggestion is recalculated as the data loads (:597). If TurfRad had nothing newer, the numbers come back unchanged (see request-scan-data/4/2).

claims.text: Dismiss closes the banner and leaves you on the data you already had — the new scan is not thrown away, it is simply not loaded yet.
claims.note: Dismiss only hides the banner. The retrieved data is already stored on the server (SpatialAdjustService.cs:2112), so nothing is thrown away.

claims.text: The banner offers Reload Data or Dismiss.
claims.note: Figure caption. The buttons are "Reload Data" (SPATIAL_ADJUST.RELOAD_DATA) and "Dismiss" (SPATIAL_ADJUST.DISMISS).

claims.text: Careful. Dismissing is not declining.
claims.note: Dismiss has no effect on the data.

claims.text: The next reload picks the new scan up.
claims.note: After Dismiss there is no Reload Data button until the next request. The data is picked up whenever the dashboard loads its data again: opening or refreshing the page, saving a settings change, or changing station factors (sa-dashboard.component.ts:262-278).

claims.text: If the request will not queue
claims.note: A failure to queue has its own error branch.

claims.text: A failed request says so straight away rather than silently doing nothing.
claims.note: A failed request at once shows "Request Failed" with "Unable to queue the scan data request. Please try again."

claims.text: If it keeps failing, the diagnostics dialog reports whether the organisation has TurfRad access and whether it has scan data at all — a course-wide problem is almost always there rather than in your settings.
claims.note: The TurfRad panel lists "TR org ID:", "TR selected course ID:", "SA has org access:", "Org has scan data:" and "Last scan date:" (sa-diagnostics-dlg.component.html:17-41). They are checked live when the dialog opens (sa-diagnostics-dlg.component.ts:61-89). These explain a course whose scans never arrive. They do not explain a request that will not queue: the server fails the request only when the site has no Spatial Adjust update record (SpatialAdjustService.cs:985-990) or the call itself fails, and Diagnostics shows neither. The Diagnostics dialog opens only on a Shift+Alt click on the Spatial Adjust logo, and only once a Lynx course is loaded or Lynx has failed to load (sa-main-toolbar.component.html:4, sa-main-toolbar.component.ts:293-299). No guide step says how to open it. Its labels are hard-coded English (sa-diagnostics-dlg.component.html:22-89).

claims.text: Diagnostics: TurfRad access, scan data, last scan date.
claims.note: Figure caption. The Diagnostics dialog opens only on a Shift+Alt click on the Spatial Adjust logo, and only once a Lynx course is loaded or Lynx has failed to load (sa-main-toolbar.component.html:4, sa-main-toolbar.component.ts:293-299). No guide step says how to open it. Its labels are hard-coded English (sa-diagnostics-dlg.component.html:22-89).

claims.text: You know the toolbar can request a scan, not only display the last one.
claims.note: Same finding as request-scan-data/tile/2.
claims.correction: You know the toolbar can fetch the latest scan data from TurfRad, not only display what was last retrieved. Why: the button brings the scheduled retrieval forward (SpatialAdjustService.cs:978-1002). It does not order a scan.

claims.text: You can tell Request latest scan data from Reload Data.
claims.note: Achievable from the guide.

claims.text: You know Dismiss leaves the dashboard on the data it already had.
claims.note: Achievable from the guide.
